trich.han: 年為根月為苗日為花時為實
trich.y: The year is the root, the month the sprout, the day the flower, the hour the fruit.

trich.han: 以年為本為父月為兄弟僚友日為主為妻為己身時為子孫
trich.y: The year is the base and the father; the month is siblings and colleagues; the day is oneself and one's spouse; the hour is children and grandchildren.

trich.han: 四柱各管年限年管十五失之太早時管五十後失之太遲
trich.y: Each pillar governs a span of years: the year pillar up to about age 15, the hour pillar from about age 50.

tuoi.ghi_chu: The book only gives the two ends: the year pillar up to about 15, the hour pillar from about 50. The two middle pillars share ages 16–49 (we do not split what the book does not split).

hop.01: your roots and the place you grew up support each other; home and early surroundings tend to point the same way.
hop.02: your roots support you; what you learned from grandparents and parents easily becomes your own capital.
hop.03: early life and later life connect; what you received from family tends to pass on to those after you.
hop.12: parents, siblings and you tend to stand on the same side; work and home rarely pull against each other.
hop.13: the effort of your younger years tends to leave lasting results later on.
hop.23: you and those who come after you (children, students, juniors) understand each other easily.

xung.01: your roots and the place you grew up pull in two directions; you often choose between family ways and your own path. Tell your family about your choices early.
xung.02: your roots and you move at different paces; you tend to leave old ways to stand on your own. Keep in regular touch with home even from afar.
xung.03: what you were used to as a child does not transfer as is to those after you. Let the next generation choose their own way.
xung.12: work, family and you often bump into each other; changes of job or home come easily. Keep some personal space and speak up early about disagreements.
xung.13: the work of your younger years and your long-term plans often change direction. Write down long-term goals and review them every year.
xung.23: you and those after you often move at different paces. Make time to listen to each other and avoid imposing your way.

hinh.01: your roots and the place you grew up rub quietly; some things at home were never said. Untangle small things one at a time instead of letting them pile up.
hinh.02: you tend to be hard on yourself by your family's standards. Set your own standard, one that fits you.
hinh.03: expectations from your roots can weigh on those who come after you. Put expectations into words and listen to the reply.
hinh.12: work and home rub lightly but for a long time. Keep work hours and home hours clearly apart.
hinh.13: current work and later plans tend to step on each other. Finish one thing before opening the next.
hinh.23: small but lasting tension can build between you and those after you. Speak plainly and gently, early.

hai.01: your roots and the place you grew up easily misread each other's expectations. Ask again before assuming.
hai.02: what your family hopes for and what you want often diverge. Show what you want through concrete actions.
hai.03: early-life and later-life expectations tend to drift apart. Write down what you want to pass on.
hai.12: family, colleagues and you easily have small misunderstandings. Confirm important things in writing.
hai.13: later plans easily drift from what you are doing now. Review your plans every quarter.
hai.23: you and those after you easily misread each other. Ask before drawing conclusions.

pha.01: family life in childhood tends to be interrupted, such as moving house or changing schools. Keep the long friendships you have.
pha.02: your work tends to be interrupted midway. Break big tasks into short stages.
pha.03: long-range plans tend to be interrupted. Keep a backup plan for long projects.
pha.12: work and home tend to cut into each other. Keep dedicated time for each.
pha.13: current work and later plans tend to cut into each other. Finish what is unfinished first.
pha.23: shared plans with those after you tend to stall. Set a concrete new date each time something is left unfinished.

cap.tu_hinh: the same character repeats and rubs against itself: you tend to blame yourself and make things hard for yourself here. Compare yourself less with yourself.

chi_lap.4: All four bottom characters are {chi}: the part about {nhom_y} runs through the whole chart.

can_lap.3: {can} appears three times in the top row: the part about {nhom_y} is what others see most in you.
